projects.subtitle: What I build off-hours — and what I'm proud of.

piton.name: Piton
piton.tagline: A Ukrainian programming language with a homegrown interpreter
piton.description: A lightweight interpreted language with an authentic Ukrainian syntax (in transliteration). Recursive descent parser, tree-walking evaluator, native SVG flowchart generation, Turing-complete. Written from scratch in Go, no yacc/bison. The interpreter is compiled to WebAssembly via TinyGo — 220 KB instead of 24 MB, runs entirely in the browser.

gomonobanksdk.title: go-monobank-sdk
gomonobanksdk.subtitle: Go SDK for every monobank API
gomonobanksdk.description: Full coverage of personal, provider (with monoКЕП), business for legal entities, acquiring (subscriptions, monopay button, split-receivers, T2P) and Installment Purchases. ECDSA webhook verification with auto-rotating keys, drop-in http.Handler, typed money/currency/MCC, HMAC-SHA256 for installment callbacks, a fake monobank server for tests, and a separate OpenTelemetry sub-module.

monokasa.title: monokasa
monokasa.subtitle: Telegram bot for selling tickets
monokasa.description: Sells tickets to a single show through a monobank jar and issues PDFs with QR codes scanned at the venue entrance. Live consumer of my own go-monobank-sdk: webhook auto-registers at startup, reservations get a 15-minute hold, and show-time reminders fire at-most-once even across restarts.

shminer.description: Cross-platform miner on Wails (Go + Svelte/TS). Rewrote SHA-256 from JS to Go with a goroutine worker pool — 1000× faster hashrate on identical hardware. AES-encrypted wallet, real-time WebSocket dashboard, multi-wallet, zen mode.

bench.title: JS vs Go·WASM — same hash, two engines
bench.subtitle: Same SHA-256, same input, two engines. Left: a JS copy of the official Student Hryvnia client. Right: my Go rewrite from SHMiner, compiled to WASM with TinyGo. Lanes run sequentially, 10 seconds each — JS first on a single core, then Go·WASM on N cores. Each lane gets the full CPU to itself, so the numbers stay honest.
bench.speedupBody: that's how much faster Go·WASM is than the official JS miner on your machine — in this configuration
bench.jsModeOriginalHint: verbatim from the official client — with `sleep(1)` every 1000 hashes
bench.disclaimer: Runs on your machine in your browser. The JS lane is single-threaded — a verbatim copy of `calculateBlockHash` from the official client (`await window.crypto.subtle.digest`, optionally + `sleep(1)` every 1000 hashes). The Go·WASM lane spins up a pool of Web Workers — one per core, just like SHMiner's goroutine pool. Difficulty is 20 bits (5 leading zero hex chars), the SHMiner default.
bench.desktopNoteBody: Native Go from the desktop client is much faster than TinyGo·WASM in the browser — native Go's SHA-256 uses SIMD/AVX CPU instructions (4-8 blocks in parallel; scalar WASM does 0), and Web Workers pay for serialization. The real numbers (1000×+ vs the official JS miner) only show up in the actual SHMiner. The Wails app is cross-platform: Linux · macOS · Windows.
